directive: Valerius commissions an exceptionally intricate and durable personal shield, deliberately making it more intricate than his weapons as a symbol of devotion to protection and defense; he further makes the double-reinforced pilum a testament to his oath to march at the head of every battle and personally participate, with a truthful combat record that can develop into a kill count only from confirmed future actions.

events.title: VALERIUS COMMISSIONS A SHIELD WORTHY OF HIS OATH
events.body: Valerius commissions a shield unlike any piece of equipment previously made for him, ordering that its protection and workmanship exceed the ornamentation of his already exceptional weapons. He deliberately tells the smiths that the shield is to be the more intricate of the two, because a weapon may end a fight but a shield exists to preserve the life behind it. The finest materials his personal mines and estate stores can provide are selected, and the work is entrusted to the most accomplished smiths and armorers attached to his estate. Its construction is planned around toughness first, with layered reinforcement and carefully fitted defensive elements beneath an elaborate Roman exterior. The commission becomes a material expression of Valerius's stated devotion to protecting himself and the men who march beside him.

events.title: THE SHIELD IS BUILT AS A DEFENSIVE MASTERWORK
events.body: The shield takes shape under repeated inspection, with its frame, facing, grip, reinforcement, and protective fittings tested separately before the final assembly. Valerius rejects the idea that greater ornament should mean greater fragility, requiring every intricate feature to remain subordinate to the shield's ability to absorb and withstand punishment. The smiths therefore build its decoration into the structure rather than simply attaching it to the surface. Roman forms remain recognizable, but the materials and workmanship make the finished object distinctly Valerian. The personal guard watches the process closely, understanding that their commander has chosen to make his principal defensive symbol more elaborate than the weapons intended to kill.

events.title: THE SHIELD BECOMES MORE INTRICATE THAN THE WEAPONS
events.body: When the shield is brought to its final finishing stage, Valerius orders its craftsmanship to exceed that of his gladius and pilum in visible intricacy. Fine work is concentrated around the rim, fittings, grip, and protective face while the underlying structure remains deliberately severe and durable. The contrast is intentional: his sword and pilum represent the means by which he can fight, while the shield represents the reason he intends to survive the fight. Veterans such as Titus Varenus and Lucius Atilius are among those who examine the finished work and recognize that the hierarchy is deliberate rather than decorative. The shield becomes the clearest physical statement yet of the household's defensive creed.

events.title: THE OATH IS SET INTO THE PILUM
events.body: Valerius orders the double-reinforced pilum to carry the substance of a new standing oath: when battle comes, he will march at the head of it rather than remain behind his men. He further declares that he will personally participate in every battle in which his command is engaged, accepting the same immediate danger that he asks his soldiers to face. The smiths preserve the oath alongside the weapon's existing record of confirmed shield-piercings, making the pilum a physical reminder of both survival and obligation. The declaration is repeated before members of the personal guard, who hear their commander's promise directly rather than through a later report. No new battle is created by the oath, but the weapon's meaning changes from specialized equipment into a personal standard of conduct.

events.title: THE PILUM'S RECORD BECOMES A CHRONICLE OF COMBAT
events.body: The surviving record attached to Valerius's pilum is reorganized so that confirmed shield-piercings remain individually traceable instead of being reduced to an unsupported aggregate. Alongside them, the weapon's future combat record is prepared to receive confirmed individual kills when they actually occur. The distinction matters to the smiths and veterans: a claim is not entered merely because a battle is remembered, and an enemy is not counted without a reliable basis in the campaign record. The result resembles a kill ledger without fabricating a number that the present record cannot prove. The pilum therefore begins to acquire a reputation of its own, associated with the commander who carries it and with the oath that he has publicly bound to it.

events.title: THE WEAPONS BEGIN TO CARRY NAMES OF THEIR OWN
events.body: The completed shield and the marked pilum produce an unexpected change in how the personal guard speaks about Valerius's equipment. Veterans begin referring to the shield as the embodiment of his protection and to the pilum as the weapon that will always be seen at the front when fighting begins. The gladius acquires a parallel reputation as the close weapon carried by the same commander, and the three pieces increasingly become recognized together rather than as ordinary equipment. Titus Varenus and Lucius Atilius are among the first to use the descriptions openly, turning private workshop symbolism into a shared guard tradition. No new kill is claimed and no battle is invented, but the weapons themselves begin to acquire a reputation within the household.

events.title: VALERIUS TAKES THE SHIELD AND SWEARS THE OATH BEFORE HIS GUARD
events.body: Valerius finally takes the completed shield into his own hands and tests its balance, grip, and defensive coverage alongside the gladius and double-reinforced pilum. He presents the shield as the greater work of craftsmanship by deliberate choice, telling the assembled guard that protection is not secondary to victory but the condition that allows victory to be carried through. He then renews his oath in their presence: when the next battle comes, he will march at its head and participate in it personally. The pilum remains the physical record of that promise, while its combat ledger is left open for future confirmed entries rather than filled with invented victories. The guard leaves the presentation with a clear image of their commander's equipment: the shield as protection, the gladius as the close blade, and the pilum as the oath-bearing weapon whose reputation will grow only through what is actually survived and proven.
